name: Broadway Comedy Club
description: Bi-level club near Times Square with three showrooms — a 225-seat main room, a 70-seat theater, and a 60-seat cafe room — running stand-up nightly.

name: Comedy Village
description: Two-showroom club opened in 2024 running stand-up seven nights a week.

name: The Grisly Pear Midtown
description: Comedian-booked comedy room attached to a bar, running multiple stand-up showcases nightly; sister room to the MacDougal St original.

name: Stones Comedy Club
description: Intimate second-floor comedy room above The Overlook Bar near Grand Central, running stand-up Wednesday through Saturday.

name: The Buddha Room (Laughing Buddha Comedy)
description: Laughing Buddha's home room above the Blarney Stone — daily registered open mics, classes, and weekly ticketed showcases.

name: Gotham Comedy Club
description: Long-running ~300-seat Chelsea club opened in 1996, known for TV tapings, its New Talent Show, and big-name drop-ins.

name: The Comedy Shop
description: Intimate basement showroom opened in 2023, running stand-up showcases seven nights a week.

name: Greenwich Village Comedy Club
description: Small cellar showroom running nightly stand-up showcases with rotating pro lineups.

name: Grisly Pear Comedy Club
description: Back-room comedy club inside a MacDougal St pub, booked by comics for comics; featured on HBO's Crashing.

name: The Comedy Cellar
description: NYC's most famous stand-up club since 1982 — rotating multi-comic lineups nightly and frequent unannounced celebrity drop-ins.

name: Village Underground
description: The Comedy Cellar's larger sister showroom, presenting Cellar stand-up exclusively seven nights a week.

name: New York Comedy Club — East Village
description: East Village outpost of New York Comedy Club, a classic brick-wall room with nightly showcases and headliner shows.

name: St. Marks Comedy Club
description: Speakeasy-style room hidden behind an art bookstore — the city's only Latino-owned comedy club, with nightly stand-up.

name: The Stand
description: Two-level restaurant and comedy club with a downstairs showroom that books A-list headliners; no drink minimum.

name: The Fear City Comedy Club
description: A 60-seat alcohol-free theater in a former boxing gym, no drink minimums, daily open mics alongside showcases.

name: Sesh Comedy
description: BYOB-friendly underground indie club running fast-paced seven-comic showcases; a free drink comes with each ticket.

name: UCB Theatre New York
description: Upright Citizens Brigade's flagship improv and sketch theater, reopened in 2024 — home of ASSSSCAT and nightly improv, sketch, and stand-up.

name: Asylum NYC
description: Comedy theater in the former PIT flagship space running stand-up, improv, sketch, and comedic musicals.

name: Magnet Theater
description: Improv and sketch theater and training center running shows seven nights a week.

name: Caveat
description: 110-seat basement theater and bar dedicated to nerdy comedy — stand-up, game shows, science-comedy, and musicals.

name: The Peoples Improv Theater (The PIT)
description: Improv and sketch theater and training center running the PIT Loft plus Lab and Fishbowl rooms at 154–156 W 29th St, seven days a week.

name: New York Comedy Club — Midtown
description: Classic ~100-seat stand-up club running nightly pro showcases with frequent big-name drop-ins.

name: New York Comedy Club — Upper West Side
description: NYCC's third Manhattan room, opened 2024 in the former Stand Up NY space; keeps the room's open-mic tradition.

name: Comic Strip Live
description: NYC's longest-running stand-up showroom (since 1976) — early proving ground for Eddie Murphy, Seinfeld, and Chris Rock.

name: Rodney's Comedy Club
description: Opened 2023 on the historic Dangerfield's stage — a ~200-seat room with shows nightly plus weekend late shows.

name: West Side Comedy Club
description: Intimate basement showroom beneath Playa Betty's, known for rotating pro lineups and drop-ins from Seinfeld and Burr.

name: Comedy in Harlem
description: NYC's only Black-owned dedicated comedy club — an intimate room with full bar, food, and DJ, weekly headliner shows and two recurring open mics.

name: Stand Up NY
description: The 1986-founded club, now operating inside Bond 45 in Times Square after leaving its longtime Upper West Side home in 2024.

name: Flop House Comedy Club (Williamsburg)
description: Comedian-founded neighborhood club under the BQE, opened 2023, with no drink minimums and rotating showcase lineups.

name: Flop House Comedy Club (East Village)
description: Flop House's second room in the East Village, running indie showcases nightly.

name: Bushwick Comedy Club
description: Comedian-owned storefront club — Brooklyn's only BYOB comedy club — running nightly showcases plus the weekly Comedy Lottery.

name: EastVille Comedy Club
description: 120-seat traditional stand-up club near Barclays Center running multiple showcases nightly.

name: Greenpoint Comedy Club
description: Stand-up club opened April 2026 by comedians Jeremy Pinsly and Kayla Sossin — a ~60-seat showroom behind a front cocktail bar.

name: The Tiny Cupboard
description: Indie DIY comedy club known for cheap high-volume stand-up shows and open mics, indoors and on its famous rooftop.

name: Brooklyn Comedy Collective
description: Improv and sketch comedy theater and training center running ~30 shows a week at Eris.

name: Union Hall
description: Park Slope bar whose basement stage is one of NYC's best-known alt-comedy rooms and a regular New York Comedy Festival venue.

name: QED Astoria
description: Small woman-owned comedy and arts venue hosting 100+ events a month — daily open mics, showcases, storytelling, and classes.

name: Littlefield
description: Gowanus performance venue and one of Brooklyn's core alt-comedy stages, hosting stand-up showcases, live podcasts, and New York Comedy Festival shows.
confirmed: Verified 7/13 Claude (Kutti Gang May 2026 listing + NYCF venue); added at Kari's request

name: The Bell House
description: Big Gowanus room that anchors Brooklyn's comedy-and-podcast circuit, regularly hosting major stand-up tapings and touring comedy shows.
